newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed to firmer at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed to firmer at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly firmer on Tuesday, amid solid corporate earnings results and following the release of June retail sales data which were viewed as non-inflationary.
Technology stocks could take the early lead, after yesterday's powerful rally and ahead of second quarter earnings from chipmaker Intel Corp, analysts said.
The large-capitilization stocks, which posted only meager gains on Monday despite a surge in the Nasdaq market, could get a lift as bonds firmed after the retail sales data.
Retail sales for June rose 0.5 percent compared with a decline of 0.1 percent in May.
"The fact that there is no strong surge on the consumer side is reassuring for the inflation watch," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said.
The long bond pared its early losses to trade down 4/32 at a 6.56 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index, which had been trading in negative ground, firmed up 1.25 points to 928.10.
"Today's market should be mixed to fair," Ackerman said. "The market momentum has been slow and steady."
